newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to launch new short-term futures contract.
newsitem.headline: Germany to launch new short-term futures contract.

text.p: Germany's electronic futures exchange DTB said it would launch a new short-term debt futures contract on March 7 to reflect the German government's new shorter term issuances.

Deliverable issues into the new contract, to be called Schatz future, will be the government's new two-year Treasury notes called Bundesschatzanweisungen as well as four-year Treasury notes and five-year government bonds (Bobls) and other paper with a remaining maturity of 21 to 27 months.
The new contract will fill a hole between the one-month and three-month euromark contracts and the Bobl and Bund futures contracts.
Like the Bund futures and the Bobl futures contracts, the Schatz futures contract will have four expiry dates during each calendar year, in March, June, September and December.
Trading will be from 0700 GMT to 1630 GMT with half an hour each for pre- and post-bourse trading.
Germany last year agreed to extend its range of government debt issues to include short-term issues with maturities of under one year.

The move was long resisted as certain officials said short-dated issues could possibly chip away at the central bank's policy-making independence. But it was finally agreed to in a bid to improve Germany's standing as a financial centre in the run-up to Europe's planned monetary union.

The DTB's new contracts have however not always been successful. Several years ago, when the government promised to issue more 30-year bonds, the DTB launched a so called BUXL futures contract which was suspended in 1995 when volume in the contract dwindled as the government failed to issue more 30-year bonds.
